_comment: WHERE AN ACTOR'S FEET ARE, AND HOW HARD IT BREATHES -- authored, not
guessed. Before this file the runtime inferred the ground line by scanning
pixels and applying a global constant, and the inference was eventually
wrong about something: the golem's ground slam erupts an earth spike ~50px
BELOW its feet and Shawn's idle plants a staff ~33px below his, so a scan
for 'the lowest opaque pixel' read both as the floor and hoisted the
figures off the ground. See docs/ART_PIPELINE.md.
groundLine: pixels from the sprite canvas's BOTTOM EDGE up to the surface
the figure stands on. One value per actor, not per stance, because a
character's feet do not move relative to their own art -- only the effects
drawn around them do. That is what stops a figure jumping between poses,
and it is only meaningful because every one of an actor's stances is
sliced onto ONE shared canvas (docs/STANCE_SHEET_SPEC.md).
groundLineSource: WHO OWNS the groundLine above -- 'slicer' or
'authored'. ABSENT MEANS 'authored', so every entry written before this
field existed keeps meaning exactly what it meant: a number a person
copied off the terminal by hand, which no tool may write over.
tools/slice_actor_sheet.py writes groundLine only when the entry is
absent (a new actor: the measurement is the tool's until somebody
disagrees with it) or when this says 'slicer'. When it says 'authored'
the tool prints its own measurement and the delta and leaves the file
alone -- the disagreement is often the point, because a scan believes
whatever it finds and what it finds may be the golem's earth spike.
breath and hover are never written by any tool at all: how hard a
creature breathes and whether it flies are judgements about the art
rather than measurements of it.
StanceManifestValidationTests re-measures every actor's committed stills
and refuses a groundLine more than 8px off. An 'authored' value beyond
that is an OVERRIDE rather than a failure -- but only if the actor's
Art/**/README.md says why, in a line naming groundLine; otherwise the
test fails naming the actor, because an override nobody wrote a reason
for is indistinguishable from a stale number left by a re-slice.
breath: how hard this creature breathes, as a multiplier on the transform
breath every idle figure carries (see Domain/Stage/BreathCurve). It is the
one number here that is a JUDGEMENT rather than a measurement. Unset means
1.0 -- every stance in the game is now a single drawing, so the transform
breath is the only thing moving an idle figure and there is nothing for it
to compete with. Negative means none; nothing needs that today, a statue
would.
There are no per-stance entries because there is no per-stance timing left
to author: a still has nothing to time. What used to live here
(secondsPerFrame, impactFrame, soundFrame, loop, endHold, returns) belonged
to frame sheets, and the wind-up a still swing needs is a transform move
rather than a drawing -- see StaticStancePlayback.
Lives in Resources/ rather than ContentData/ because it is read at RUNTIME
rather than baked by ContentBuilder, and deliberately NOT under
Resources/Content/, which ContentBuilder deletes wholesale on every run.

actors._groundLineNote: Dropped from 12 to 8 when the whole actor was re-sliced onto one shared canvas; 8 is what that canvas measures, re-confirmed 2026-08-30 with every pose agreeing within 1px. Unchanged by the move to stills -- idle.png and attack.png are two of those same frames, on that same canvas.

Handed to the slicer 2026-09-06: Art/Characters/owl/recipe.json replays the six committed stills byte for byte, so this 8 is a measurement the tool can reproduce rather than a judgement. The hover below is NOT -- no tool writes it.
actors._hoverNote: Odette FLIES. hover.height is her resting altitude above the ground line in STAGE pixels and hover.bob the excursion either side of it (HoverCurve); FightController pushes it every frame in every stance but defeated, and the animator composes it with lunges and recoils. Height 70 is what lifts her body clear of the front-row figure standing in front of her far slot -- see Art/Characters/owl/README.md. All six stills stand on the same floor; nothing about the hover is baked into the drawings.

actors._groundLineNote: Re-measured 2026-09-04. Was 14, which was never a foot position at all -- it was the uniform pad around six independently cropped frames per stance, and the entry admitted to a possible vertical pop between stances because of it. The six delivered stills were recomposited onto ONE 741x499 canvas by the same ground-band anchor slice_actor_sheet.py uses, so the pop is gone and this is a measured ground line like every other entry here.

Six stills sliced from sheet_poses.png (2026-09-04), all on one 646x478 canvas; the slicer measured this ground line and every pose agrees within 0px. Handed to the slicer 2026-09-06, once Art/Enemies/treant/recipe.json was shown to replay the committed stills byte for byte -- a measurement a tool can reproduce is a measurement that tool should own.
